title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
statement: Given a list of positive integers and a target, return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least the target, or 0 if none exists.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(2)
    return [400000, [r.randint(1, 10) for _ in range(100000)]]

hints.1_question: If all numbers are positive, what happens to the sum when you add an element on the right? When you drop one on the left?
hints.2_nudge: Grow the window from the right until the sum reaches the target, then shrink from the left for as long as it still does.
hints.3_big_hint: Loop right; add nums[right]; while total >= target: record the length, subtract nums[left], left += 1. If nothing was ever recorded, return 0.

known_bugs.name: returns infinity when nothing qualifies
known_bugs.followup: What does your function return if no subarray reaches the target?

known_bugs.name: shrinks only once (if instead of while)
known_bugs.followup: After you shrink once, could the window still be valid? Could it be even shorter?

known_bugs.name: strict > instead of >=
known_bugs.followup: What happens if one element equals the target exactly? Does that window count?

followups: Each element is added once and removed at most once. Why does that make the nested loop O(n)?
Would this approach still work if the array could contain negative numbers? Why or why not?
